discoveries.title: A day on Mars is about 40 minutes longer than a day on Earth.
discoveries.body: One Martian day, called a sol, lasts 24 hours, 39 minutes and 35 seconds.

discoveries.title: The sky around the Sun looks blue on Mars.
discoveries.body: Dust in the Martian atmosphere scatters blue light forward toward the observer much more efficiently, so a blueish halo is always seen close to the Sun.

source.name: NASA Science, The Sun Sets on Mars

quiz.question: What is the name of the largest volcano in the solar system, located on Mars?
quiz.explanation: Olympus Mons is the largest known volcano in the solar system: about 27 kilometers high and over 600 kilometers wide at its base.

discoveries.title: On Mars you would weigh only about 38 percent of your Earth weight.
discoveries.body: Mars has about a tenth of Earth's mass, so its gravity is only 38 percent as strong as ours. Someone who weighs 60 kilograms on Earth would weigh the equivalent of about 23 kilograms there.

discoveries.title: Mars has two tiny moons called Fear and Terror.
discoveries.body: Phobos and Deimos, named after the Greek words for fear and terror, are irregularly shaped and each only a few miles across.

discoveries.title: Mars in short
discoveries.body: Mars is about half the size of Earth and twice the size of our Moon. It circles the Sun once every 687 Earth days. Its thin atmosphere is about 95 percent carbon dioxide, and the average surface temperature is around minus 53 degrees Celsius.

discoveries.title: The Moon is, on average, 384,400 kilometers from Earth.
discoveries.body: Its orbit is not a perfect circle: the distance changes from about 363,300 km at the closest point to about 405,500 km at the farthest.

source.name: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive, Moon Fact Sheet

discoveries.title: We always see the same side of the Moon.
discoveries.body: The Moon spins in exactly the time it takes to orbit Earth, so it never turns its back to us. Satellites have shown us the side we cannot see.

discoveries.title: How strong is gravity on the Moon?

quiz.question: How strong is gravity on the Moon compared with Earth?
quiz.explanation: Gravity at the Moon's surface is about one-sixth of Earth's, so an astronaut weighs about six times less there than at home.

discoveries.title: The Moon is less than a third as wide as Earth.
discoveries.body: Its radius is about 1,740 kilometers (1,080 miles).

discoveries.title: The Moon most likely formed after a Mars-sized body hit Earth.
discoveries.body: NASA says this collision probably happened several billion years ago.

discoveries.title: The Moon in short
discoveries.body: The Moon is about 384,400 km away and less than a third as wide as Earth. It orbits Earth in about 27 days and always shows us the same side. Gravity on its surface is one-sixth of Earth's.

discoveries.title: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach Earth.
discoveries.body: The Sun is about 150 million kilometers (93 million miles) away, so we always see it as it was a few minutes ago.

source.name: NASA Space Place, All About the Sun

discoveries.title: It would take about 1.3 million Earths to fill the Sun.
discoveries.body: The Sun is about 100 times wider than Earth and about 10 times wider than Jupiter, the biggest planet.

discoveries.title: How much of the solar system's mass is in the Sun?

quiz.question: How much of the solar system's mass is in the Sun?
quiz.explanation: The Sun holds 99.8 percent of the solar system's mass, so every planet, moon and asteroid together share the remaining 0.2 percent.

discoveries.title: The surface of the Sun is about 5,500 degrees Celsius.
discoveries.body: Its core is far hotter: temperatures there top 15 million degrees Celsius.

discoveries.title: The Sun spins faster at its equator than at its poles.
discoveries.body: It turns once about every 25 Earth days at the equator and once about every 36 Earth days at the poles.

discoveries.title: The Sun in short
discoveries.body: The Sun is a yellow dwarf star, a huge ball of hydrogen and helium about 1.4 million km across. It holds 99.8 percent of the solar system's mass, and its core is hotter than 15 million degrees Celsius.
